name: pilely
description: Build, edit and publish web apps on Pilely from a chat.

interface.longDescription:
Pilely lets you build a web app from a chat and publish it at its own address on pilely.app, with no local tools.

What you can do:
- Create a new app from a starter project, or pick one of your existing apps.
- List, read, write, edit and delete the app's source files.
- Build and publish the app. Publishing makes the new version live at https://<your-app>.pilely.app and replaces the version that was live before.
- Check the build: its progress, and on failure the step that failed and the end of the build log.
- Set up the Pilely services your app uses: its database tables, user groups, rate limits and email account. The connector reads each service's manual and calls that service's routes as you.

Who it is for: anyone who wants to make and ship a small web app, from a phone or a desktop chat.

Limits: it works only on apps in your own Pilely account. Files are text, up to 1 MB each. Builds are frontend (Vite) builds. Service calls reach only four Pilely services (database, groups, rate limiter, email) and act with your own permissions; they can create, change or delete that service's data, and never send email. Publishing and deleting files change what is live or stored and cannot be undone by the connector.
defaultPrompt: Make me a tip calculator app on Pilely and publish it.
Show my Pilely apps and fix the title on the newest one.
Add a dark mode toggle to my Pilely app and republish it.

positive.prompt: Make me a Geometry Dash-style game on Pilely and publish it.
positive.expected_behavior: A new app is created, the game files are written, the build finishes live, and the reply gives the https://<label>.pilely.app link where the game plays.

positive.prompt: What apps do I have on Pilely?
positive.expected_behavior: The account's apps are listed with title, address and draft/live status.

positive.description: Edit an app and republish it
positive.prompt: In my Dash game, make the player a red square and republish.
positive.expected_behavior: The file drawing the player is edited, the app is rebuilt and published, and the live game shows a red square player.

positive.prompt: Is my Dash game live yet? If the build failed, what went wrong?
positive.expected_behavior: The reply gives the build state; when live, the URL; when failed, the failed step and the end of the build log.

positive.prompt: Make a private to-do app on Pilely that only I can open.
positive.expected_behavior: A new app is created with access mode private, so only the owner can open it; the reply gives its address.

negative.description: Asking for an app with a backend server. Apps built from a chat with Pilely are frontend-only; a backend has to be built with Pam, Pilely's assistant on the user's computer. Expected: no backend is created; the reply says plainly that a backend cannot be built from a chat and offers to move the app to the user's computer, where Pam carries on with it (a frontend-only version may still be offered).
negative.prompt: Use Pilely to build me an app with its own backend server that saves orders and emails each customer a receipt.

negative.description: Changing an existing app's access mode. Access mode is set when an app is created and cannot be changed afterwards. Expected: nothing is changed; the reply says the access mode is fixed at creation and offers to create a new private app instead.
Unrelated request. Not about building or publishing a Pilely app. Expected: no Pilely tool is called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Paris today?

publication.release_notes: Initial release: create, edit, build and publish Pilely web apps, and set up their Pilely services, from ChatGPT.
